flowers.name: ★ State Flower: Rocky Mountain Columbine
flowers.habitat: State symbol
flowers.wildlife: State symbol — see full entry.
flowers.description: Colorado's breathtaking state flower — large blue-and-white two-toned flowers with long nectar spurs, one of North America's most beautiful wildflowers.

flowers.name: Rocky Mountain Columbine
flowers.habitat: Mountain meadows, rocky slopes, aspen groves, subalpine zones
flowers.wildlife: Hummingbird nectar plant. Long-tongued bumblebees reach nectar. Hawkmoths pollinate at night — the long spurs accommodate them.
flowers.description: Colorado's state flower and one of North America's most beautiful wildflowers — large blue sepals and white petals with dramatically long backwards-pointing blue spurs. Found from foothills to 11,000 feet. Protected by law in Colorado — never collect from wild. Self-seeds readily in mountain gardens.

flowers.name: Indian Paintbrush (Wyoming)
flowers.habitat: Dry mountain slopes, sagebrush, pinyon-juniper woodland
flowers.wildlife: Critical hummingbird nectar source in the mountains. Semi-parasitic on sagebrush and other plants.
flowers.description: Colorado's most common native paintbrush — brilliant scarlet to orange bracts on slender stems above sagebrush and rocky mountain slopes. Wyoming's state flower. Semi-parasitic on neighboring plants making transplanting difficult. One of the most dramatic wildflowers of the Rocky Mountain landscape.

flowers.name: Colorado Blue Columbine
flowers.habitat: Alpine and subalpine rocky slopes, high elevation
flowers.wildlife: Adapted for bumblebee and hummingbird pollination at high elevation.
flowers.description: A tiny high-altitude columbine found above treeline in Colorado's alpine zone — barely 6 inches tall but with perfectly formed blue-and-white flowers. A marvel of alpine adaptation, blooming just weeks after snowmelt in Colorado's harshest environments.

flowers.name: Subalpine Larkspur
flowers.habitat: Subalpine meadows, aspen groves, moist mountain slopes
flowers.wildlife: Hummingbird nectar plant in high mountain meadows. Bumblebee forage at altitude.
flowers.description: Tall spikes of deep blue-purple flowers towering 6 feet in Colorado's subalpine meadows. Creates spectacular drifts alongside columbine and paintbrush. One of the signature wildflowers of the Colorado Rockies above 9,000 feet. Toxic to cattle — actually protects mountain meadows from overgrazing.

flowers.name: Prairie Coneflower
flowers.habitat: Dry prairies, roadsides, disturbed areas, foothills
flowers.wildlife: Native bee forage. Seeds eaten by birds. Drought tolerant across Colorado's varied elevations.
flowers.description: The yellow Mexican Hat coneflower of Colorado's eastern plains and foothills — drooping yellow petals around a tall brown thimble. Bridges Colorado's two worlds: equally at home on eastern shortgrass prairie and western foothills. Extremely drought tolerant. Long blooming season through the hot Colorado summer.

flowers.name: ★ State Flower: Sego Lily
flowers.habitat: State symbol
flowers.wildlife: State symbol — see full entry.
flowers.description: Utah's state flower and a symbol of survival — the Sego Lily's bulbs sustained Mormon pioneers and Native peoples through famine.

flowers.name: Sego Lily
flowers.habitat: Dry grassland, sagebrush, pinyon-juniper woodland
flowers.wildlife: Native bee pollen source. Bulbs eaten by bears, rodents, and historically by humans.
flowers.description: Utah's exquisite state flower — three cupped white petals with a yellow center and purple marking. Chosen as state flower because the bulbs saved Mormon settlers from starvation during their first difficult winters. The Paiute and Ute peoples used the bulbs as a staple food. Flowers from a small bulb in dry, seemingly inhospitable terrain.

flowers.name: Cliffrose
flowers.habitat: Rocky canyon walls, mesas, desert shrubland
flowers.wildlife: Critical deer and pronghorn browse. Nesting site for many birds. Fragrant flowers attract native bees.
flowers.description: Intensely fragrant white rose-like flowers cover this sprawling evergreen shrub that clings to Utah's canyon walls and rocky mesas. Named for explorer Howard Stansbury. The bark was used by Navajo and Hopi peoples for weaving sandals and clothing. Feathery seed plumes persist through winter.

flowers.name: Utah Penstemon
flowers.habitat: Desert shrubland, rocky slopes, canyon rims
flowers.wildlife: Essential hummingbird nectar plant in Utah's canyon country. Also visited by sphinx moths.
flowers.description: Brilliant scarlet tubular flowers on upright stems in Utah's canyon country. One of the most striking of all penstemons — the vivid red color specifically adapted for hummingbird pollination. Blooms when Broad-tailed Hummingbirds arrive in spring. Thrives in rocky soil and extreme heat.

flowers.name: Desert Marigold
flowers.habitat: Sandy desert, washes, roadsides, disturbed ground
flowers.wildlife: Native bee forage. Drought tolerant. Deer resistant.
flowers.description: Woolly silver-grey foliage crowned with bright yellow daisy flowers blooming nearly year-round in Utah's warm desert valleys. One of the longest-blooming native wildflowers — nearly continuous bloom from spring through fall. Creates striking silver-and-gold mounds in desert gardens. Self-seeds freely.

flowers.name: Firecracker Penstemon
flowers.habitat: Rocky desert slopes, canyon walls, sandy washes
flowers.wildlife: Major hummingbird nectar plant — one of the first spring flowers for arriving hummingbirds. Also attracts Anna's Hummingbird in winter.
flowers.description: Bright red tubular flowers in dense clusters on stiff stems — the most hummingbird-adapted penstemon in Utah. Blooms in early spring before most desert plants. Extremely drought tolerant once established. Evergreen basal leaves remain through winter. The red flowers are invisible to most insects but irresistible to hummingbirds.

flowers.name: ★ State Flower: Indian Paintbrush
flowers.habitat: State symbol
flowers.wildlife: State symbol — see full entry.
flowers.description: Wyoming's state flower — the Indian Paintbrush, whose brilliant scarlet bracts paint Wyoming's mountain meadows red through the summer.

flowers.name: Indian Paintbrush
flowers.habitat: Mountain meadows, sagebrush steppe, dry slopes
flowers.wildlife: Critical hummingbird nectar source. Broad-tailed and Rufous Hummingbirds follow the bloom. Semi-parasitic on sagebrush roots.
flowers.description: Wyoming's iconic state flower — brilliant scarlet bracts (modified leaves, not petals) that look like a brush dipped in red-orange paint. Semi-parasitic on the roots of neighboring plants. Impossible to transplant but self-seeds in appropriate habitat. Turns Wyoming's mountain meadows and roadsides scarlet through summer.

flowers.name: Bitterroot
flowers.habitat: Rocky ridges, gravelly soil, dry exposed slopes
flowers.wildlife: Native bee pollen source. Seeds dispersed by ants. Named for the Bitterroot River and Bitterroot Mountains.
flowers.description: Extraordinary multi-petaled pink flowers emerging directly from rocky ground — the leaves die back before blooming. Can survive years of drought and reportedly be revived from dried herbarium specimens years after collection. Montana's state flower, also common in Wyoming's mountains. Among the most spectacular of all Rocky Mountain wildflowers.

flowers.name: Wyoming Paintbrush
flowers.habitat: Mountain slopes, sagebrush desert, alpine zones
flowers.wildlife: Hummingbird nectar. The yellow paintbrush is rarer and more spectacular than the common scarlet form.
flowers.description: Wyoming's yellow-flowered paintbrush — a striking variant that creates gasps from hikers accustomed to seeing only red. Grows from sage flats to alpine zones. Semi-parasitic like all paintbrushes. Often overlooked because it lacks the red color, but equally beautiful against the grey-green sagebrush.

flowers.name: Sticky Geranium
flowers.habitat: Mountain meadows, open woodland, moist slopes
flowers.wildlife: Native bee and bumblebee forage. Bees have to avoid sticky stems to reach nectar.
flowers.description: Large pink-lavender five-petaled flowers on sticky-stemmed plants in Wyoming's mountain meadows and forest edges. One of the most beautiful and common wildflowers of the Rockies. The sticky hairs on stems and leaves trap and deter insects from climbing up to steal nectar without pollinating. Long blooming season.

flowers.name: Mule's Ears
flowers.habitat: Mountain meadows, sagebrush, open slopes
flowers.wildlife: Major native bee forage. Seeds eaten by birds. Deer browse the large leaves. Named for Nathaniel Wyeth.
flowers.description: Large bright yellow sunflower-like flowers above enormous glossy dark green leaves that persist all season — the big 'mule ear' leaves are unmistakable. Turns mountain meadows gold in late spring. Named for explorer Nathaniel Wyeth. Spreads slowly by rhizomes to form large colonies.

flowers.name: ★ State Flower: Saguaro Blossom
flowers.habitat: State symbol
flowers.wildlife: State symbol — see full entry.
flowers.description: Arizona's state flower — the large white waxy blooms of the Saguaro cactus, appearing only at night and pollinated by bats.

flowers.name: Saguaro Cactus
flowers.habitat: Sonoran Desert, rocky slopes below 4,000ft, south-facing slopes
flowers.wildlife: Gila Woodpeckers excavate nesting holes used by dozens of other species. White-winged Doves and Lesser Long-nosed Bats are primary pollinators. Fruit eaten by 100+ species including coyotes, javelinas, and many birds.
flowers.description: Arizona's iconic symbol — a slow-growing giant reaching 40 feet and 150+ years old. The large white waxy flowers open only at night in late spring, pollinated by lesser long-nosed bats. The living embodiment of the Sonoran Desert. A single mature saguaro is an entire ecosystem. Protected by state law.

flowers.name: Mexican Poppy
flowers.habitat: Desert grassland, disturbed desert soil, roadsides
flowers.wildlife: Native bee and butterfly forage. Mass blooms after good winter rains create spectacular color.
flowers.description: Brilliant orange poppy flowers that carpet Arizona's desert grasslands and roadsides after winter rains. Closely related to the California Poppy. In peak 'superbloom' years after exceptional rainfall, Arizona roadsides and hillsides turn orange for miles. Each flower closes at night and in overcast weather.

flowers.name: Desert Mariposa Lily
flowers.habitat: Desert grassland, rocky slopes, Joshua tree woodland
flowers.wildlife: Native bee pollen source. A rare and spectacular desert wildflower.
flowers.description: Extraordinary vermillion to orange-red cupped flowers with purple markings in Arizona's desert grassland and rocky slopes. One of the most vivid and unexpected wildflowers of the Southwest — the intense orange-red color stands out dramatically against desert brown. Protected — never collect from wild.

flowers.name: Penstemon (Arizona)
flowers.habitat: Rocky desert slopes, canyon walls, disturbed desert soil
flowers.wildlife: Major hummingbird nectar plant. Also visited by sphinx moths.
flowers.description: Hot pink to magenta tubular flowers on large shrubby plants on Arizona's rocky desert slopes. One of the most spectacular of all penstemons — blooming profusely in spring. The intense color and shape are hummingbird adaptations. Native to the Sonoran and Chihuahuan Desert zones.

flowers.name: Desert Marigold
flowers.habitat: Sandy desert, washes, roadsides
flowers.wildlife: Native bee forage. Deer resistant. Long blooming season.
flowers.description: Woolly silver-grey mounds crowned with bright yellow daisy flowers — one of Arizona's longest-blooming natives, flowering nearly year-round in warmer areas. Self-seeds freely along desert roadsides. The silver foliage reflects heat, an elegant desert adaptation. Toxic to sheep — avoids being grazed.

flowers.name: ★ State Flower: Yucca Flower
flowers.habitat: State symbol
flowers.wildlife: State symbol — see full entry.
flowers.description: New Mexico's state flower — the creamy white bell-shaped flowers of yucca, pollinated exclusively by yucca moths in one of nature's most specific partnerships.

flowers.name: Soaptree Yucca
flowers.habitat: Chihuahuan Desert, grassland, sandy flats
flowers.wildlife: Pollinated exclusively by yucca moths (Tegeticula) in a 40-million-year-old co-evolutionary relationship — neither can reproduce without the other. White-winged Doves eat seeds. Javelinas eat the base.
flowers.description: New Mexico's state flower — tall stalks of creamy white bell-shaped flowers rising 10-15 feet from spiky rosettes. The most spectacular of the yuccas. Pollinated only by a single moth species in one of nature's most elegant partnerships. The saponin-rich roots were used as soap and shampoo by many Southwestern peoples.

flowers.name: Claret Cup Cactus
flowers.habitat: Rocky slopes, canyon walls, piñon-juniper woodland
flowers.wildlife: The most important hummingbird nectar plant among cacti. Hummingbirds follow the bloom northward in spring. Fruit (strawberry cactus) edible — eaten by many animals.
flowers.description: One of the most beautiful cacti in New Mexico — brilliant scarlet flowers covering the entire surface of clumping cylindrical stems in spring. Evolved specifically for hummingbird pollination — the red color, tubular shape, and lack of landing platform are all hummingbird adaptations. Fruits are sweet and edible.

flowers.name: Scarlet Gilia (Skyrocket)
flowers.habitat: Dry mountain slopes, pinyon-juniper, ponderosa pine zone
flowers.wildlife: Primary hummingbird nectar plant in New Mexico's mountains. Broad-tailed Hummingbird timed to coincide with bloom.
flowers.description: Spectacular red tubular flowers on slender stems in New Mexico's mountain zone — one of the most dramatic hummingbird plants in the Southwest. The intense red color and narrow tube evolved for hummingbird pollination. Can change flower color from red to pink or white if hummingbirds are absent and bees become the primary pollinator.

flowers.name: Desert Willow
flowers.habitat: Desert washes, arroyos, desert grassland
flowers.wildlife: Major hummingbird nectar plant. Bee forage. Seeds eaten by birds. Not a true willow — member of the catalpa family.
flowers.description: Large orchid-like pink and purple flowers on a tree growing in desert washes and arroyos — one of New Mexico's most beautiful native trees. Blooms for months through the desert summer. The flowers are visited by hummingbirds and large bees. Long narrow leaves like a willow but related to catalpa.

flowers.name: Apache Plume
flowers.habitat: Desert slopes, rocky canyons, pinyon-juniper woodland
flowers.wildlife: Native bee forage. Feathery plumes provide nesting material for birds. Deer and pronghorn browse the plant.
flowers.description: White rose-like flowers followed by extraordinary feathery pink-tipped seed plumes that persist for months — the plant earns its name from the resemblance to an Apache warrior's feathered headdress. One of the most beautiful native shrubs of the Southwest. Drought tolerant once established.
